new: Sharp text, a test (the Debug tab, This headset, under Automatic quality; off by default): the story's text panel and play bar as WebXR layers, which the headset draws itself at the display's resolution.
Its values: layer (behind the scene, which keeps covering it), for text (the same, the headset's text filter), in front (over everything, rays and menu too) and off.
Turn it on, then start the headset view: the layers come with the session. In that session all four switch live, so you can compare with off.
A link can set it: #sharp=layer, text, front or off. #sharpsize=full if the panel shows at double size.
test: On a Quest in VR: Debug tab, Sharp text: layer. Leave the headset view and start it again. Read the story panel's small text, then press through for text, in front and off.
The same in AR, with Cards: in 3D and on top. Point at the panel: the ray and its dot should show over it (not with in front).
Grip the panel and move it, walk round it, move with the sticks, swap stories: the sharp panel should stay exactly where the panel is.
The line beside the button: how many layers show and how long a write takes. Watch the frame rate with it on and off.
untested: Everything on a real headset: whether Quest Browser accepts the layers at all, and whether the text looks sharper.
Behind the scene relies on the headset using the eye buffer's transparency: if it does not, the panel shows black in VR (in front still works).
The panel's size: the lab found Quest Browser takes half sizes. If it is double or half, try #sharpsize=full.
In AR, a real hand in front of a panel behind the scene does not hide it.
